findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no topic-user row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns `nil` for users who have not yet created a `TopicUser` record for this topic, but the next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`. Such users receive an error instead of being unsubscribed. Handle the missing row by creating a muted preference (or use the model's change helper).

findings.title: The unsubscribe action can resubscribe users and does not always mute
findings.body: This endpoint toggles notification state rather than applying an unsubscribe. A second visit changes a muted topic back to regular, so refreshing or reopening the email link reverses the user's choice. Also, a watching or tracking topic is only downgraded to regular, which does not mute it. Make the operation idempotently set the topic to muted.

findings.title: Saving the preference directly bypasses TopicUser change handling
findings.body: Calling `save!` here bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which records `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishes the notification-level change. In particular, if the reason remains `nil`, `TopicUser.update_last_read` can later auto-promote this preference to tracking, undoing the unsubscribe. Use the shared change path and set the reason as a user change.

findings.title: A GET request changes the logged-in user's notification preference
findings.body: The unsubscribe URL is a GET endpoint that mutates the current user's topic preference without a confirmation or signed per-user token. A cross-site link or embedded resource can therefore cause a logged-in user to mute a topic, and email link scanners that fetch the URL can trigger the change before the user clicks it. Avoid state changes on ordinary GET requests or require an explicit, protected confirmation.
